مَدَدٌ (S, K, &c.) ―
-b2- أَمْرُهُمْ مَدَدٌ Their affair, or case, is conformable to the just mean; like أَمَدٌ and زَمَمٌ. (TA in art. زم). ―
-b3- Aid, or succour, given to one's people in war, &c., such as an auxiliary force, and corn; (T, L;) an accession to an army, &c.; (Mgh;) a military force forming an accession to warriors in the cause of God: (L:) pl. أَمْدَادٌ only: (Sb, L:) in like manner, ↓ مَادَّةٌ signifies anything wherewith one aids a people in war, &c. (L.) ―
-b4- [A mystic aid imparted by a وَلِىّ.] ―
-b5- See مَدٌّ.
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
